name: QEMU linux-user: non-PIE ET_EXEC guest image reserved with MAP_FIXED_NOREPLACE at the ELF's own load address (i386 default 0x08048000)
component: qemu-i386 linux-user: load_elf_image, ehdr->e_type == ET_EXEC branch
required_postconditions: MAP_FIXED_NOREPLACE must actually refuse a collision; if the kernel silently degrades it to a hint, the 'extra check' the comment relies on is gone and QEMU will map the guest image over a host object
the whole ELF load range [range.lo, range.hi] is reserved in one call before any segment is mapped over it

failure_sink.description: load_addr == -1 takes 'goto exit_mmap', which reports the mmap failure and ultimately terminates the guest load. Not an assert: the error is propagated.

source_locations.symbol: comment: 'In the case of ET_EXEC, we supply MAP_FIXED_NOREPLACE so that we get exactly the address range that is required.'
comment: 'using MAP_FIXED_NOREPLACE instead of MAP_FIXED provides an extra check.'
MAP_FIXED_NOREPLACE is also the primitive probe_guest_base uses to test whether a host range is free
#ifdef __FreeBSD__ #define MAP_FIXED_NOREPLACE (MAP_FIXED | MAP_EXCL) - the same contract is spelled differently per host OS

extraction_limitations: size 1048576 is representative. The real size is range.hi - range.lo + 1, a property of the guest ELF file, not a source constant.
address 0x8048000 is the conventional i386 non-PIE link base, taken from the guest binary's p_vaddr, not from QEMU's source. QEMU adds guest_base to it before calling the host mmap.

x_campaign.rationale: The probe measured fixed_noreplace_available=true and exact placement works for free page-aligned ranges; 0x08048000 is not occupied in a normal x86-64 Linux process, whose own image sits at 0x400000 or in the 0x55.. PIE band.
x_campaign.note_after_schema_fix: QEMU maps over its PROT_NONE reservation and checks THAT call; it is not the Windows two-phase model.
